successors.name: British Africa
successors.text: the Bulozi (Barotse) Floodplain of the Zambezi and surrounding territory: 'expanded to cover the Bulozi Floodplain and surrounding territories'; the Western Province of Zambia stands in for the…

ledger.x: Around 1840: the Makololo overrun the Plain.
1878 (bridge): the late-19th-century realm of about 390,000 km2 under Lewanika (reign 1878-1916, broken 1884-85).
ledger.cp: tributary peoples between the Kwito and the Kafue (the page names none)

ledger.x: 1895: 'In 1895, the Portuguese occupied some of the Lozi's western territory' 'following the Anglo-Portuguese agreement to set their claims' borders at the Zambezi'.
1899: the Order of Council cuts the realm to Bulozi proper.
1905: the occupation of the Lozi western territory ends in its cession: 'In 1905 and 1911 respectively, the kingdom lost territory in the west to Portuguese Angola and the Caprivi Strip'.
1905: the western territory goes to Portuguese Angola.
1911: the Caprivi land goes to German South West Africa ('the Caprivi Strip (German South West Africa)'), the second of the two losses the page dates 'respectively'.
1911: the kingdom becomes a province of Northern Rhodesia.

wars.name: Lozi rising against the Makololo
wars.outcome: The Makololo dynasty falls: 'came to an end in 1864' after 'a 1863-1864 war of succession' (Makololo page); the Lozi rebellion of 1864 expelled them (Barotseland page).

certainty.note: No frontier is described before 1899; the late-19th-century extent is a size and two river names; the colonial lines of 1899-1911 are not on the pages.
